## Overview

Assessment 1 runs across the whole semester. Rather than a single submission, it assesses the practical work you produce week by week in the laboratory and practical sessions.

The purpose is to build **demonstrable technical competence** with XR hardware and toolchains, and to keep that competence evidenced as you go. Work is assessed on what you can show working on a device, not on what you describe.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Weighting | 30% |
| Type | Continuous practical evaluation |
| Submission | Individual |
| Due | Ongoing — evidenced weekly, portfolio submitted end of semester |

---

## Learning Outcomes

- **LO1:** Demonstrate a critical understanding of the concepts and principles of 3D systems and augmented and virtual reality in the context of spatial computing
- **LO2:** Explore, critique and deconstruct modern VR, AR, and spatial computing experiences
- **LO3:** Demonstrate theoretical understanding of, and practical competence in the use of advanced input and output devices and sensors in an immersive environment

---

## How It Works

Each laboratory and practical session ends with a stated deliverable — a working scene, a deployed build, a configured device, a documented comparison.

For each session you must:

1. **Complete the session deliverable** and have it signed off by your tutor before you leave.
2. **Record it in your portfolio** — a short entry with what you built, what worked, what did not, and what you changed.
3. **Commit your project files** to your student repository.

Sign-off is the primary evidence. A portfolio entry without a working deliverable behind it carries no marks.

---

## Portfolio Requirements

Maintain a single running portfolio for the semester. Each weekly entry should contain:

- the session title and date
- a screenshot, screen capture, or through-the-lens video of the working result
- a short technical note — 150 to 250 words — covering what you implemented and any problems you solved
- a link to the relevant commit or project folder

Keep entries short and specific. This is a working log, not an essay.

---

## What Is Being Assessed

| Component | Weight | What we look for |
|---|---|---|
| Technical execution | 40% | Deliverables work on the target device. Correct use of the toolchain and SDKs. |
| Consistency and engagement | 25% | Sustained weekly participation and sign-off across the semester. |
| Documentation quality | 20% | Clear, accurate, specific portfolio entries with usable evidence. |
| Problem solving | 15% | Evidence of diagnosing and resolving issues rather than avoiding them. |

---

## Marking Bands

| Band | Descriptor |
|---|---|
| 70–100 | Consistent weekly deliverables, all working on device. Confident, independent use of the toolchain. Documentation is precise and shows real diagnostic reasoning. |
| 60–69 | Most deliverables complete and working. Good technical competence with occasional gaps. Documentation is clear. |
| 50–59 | Deliverables partially complete or unreliable on device. Basic competence. Documentation thin or inconsistent. |
| Below 50 | Significant gaps in attendance or deliverables. Work does not run. Little or no usable evidence. |

---

## Practical Notes

- **Sign-off must happen in the session.** Work shown late cannot be verified against the session it belongs to.
- **Deploy to hardware wherever the session calls for it.** Editor-only results do not demonstrate LO3.
- **Missed a session?** Speak to me the same week. Catch-up is possible; silent absence is not.
- **Handle the hardware carefully** and report any damage immediately.

---

## Tips

- Capture evidence *while* the thing is working — not from memory afterwards.
- Write the technical note the same day. It takes ten minutes then and an hour later.
- Record failures as well as successes. Diagnosing a problem is assessable; hiding it is not.
- Keep your repository tidy and current. It is part of the evidence.
